headline: Instagram to demote unlabeled AI accounts pretending to be human, limiting their reach
summary: Instagram will limit the reach of AI-generated profiles that fail to self-label, preventing their posts from being recommended to non-followers in Reels and Explore. This move aims to address the rise of deceptive AI influencers.
details: Instagram is taking steps to address the rise of fake AI-influencer accounts that have become increasingly difficult to distinguish from real humans. The platform is also renaming the "AI creator" label to "AI-generated profile" to clearly indicate when a profile features an AI-generated person.

Accounts that fail to self-label their AI-generated profiles will face penalties, including limited reach. This means their posts will not be recommended to non-followers in Reels and Explore, though profile owners can appeal if wrongly flagged.

The policy specifically targets profiles that feature an AI-generated person, not general content created using AI tools. Instagram stated that users do not need to add a label for content generated with AI tools if it doesn't depict an AI-generated person.

Instagram noted that users dislike encountering profiles that appear human only to discover later that the person featured is AI-generated. The platform emphasized that people want transparency and to know when a profile showcases an AI-generated individual.

headline_marked: [[Grok 4.6 lands in Microsoft Foundry]] for C# developers, optimized for agentic workloads
headline: Grok 4.6 lands in Microsoft Foundry for C# developers, optimized for agentic workloads
summary: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 is now available in public preview as an Azure Direct Model, designed for long-horizon agentic work, robust tool calling, and delivering finished products in .NET environments.
details: Grok 4.6, SpaceXAI's frontier model, is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry as an Azure Direct Model. It's specifically built for long-horizon, agentic work, differentiating it from models focused on single-prompt responses.

This design enables Grok 4.6 to plan across multiple steps, reliably call tools, recover from errors, and produce complete work products. This capability is crucial for building robust AI agents that can handle real-world workloads.

Developers can integrate Grok 4.6 without Python, using Microsoft.Extensions.AI and dotnet run. It supports key .NET workloads, including deployment-readiness agents and complex software engineering tasks.

The model integrates seamlessly into Foundry via the IChatClient abstraction, allowing developers to swap Grok 4.6 with other models like GPT-4o with just a configuration change, not a rewrite. It's deployed from the Foundry Model Catalog.

Grok 4.6 excels in multi-step reasoning, such as combining service health and error rate checks to make informed deployment decisions. This prevents false "all clear" signals that single-signal checks might produce.

For software engineering, it supports multi-stage coding and debugging across complex repositories. This allows it to reason about changes holistically, identifying cross-file bugs that isolated reviews would miss.

The model can also transform dense source material into strongly-typed structured output. This enables applications to directly act on model recommendations, integrating them into enterprise workflows for approvals or dashboards.
With support for both text and images, Grok 4.6 simplifies document- and diagram-heavy workflows. Developers can add DataContent alongside TextContent using the same IChatClient and message pattern.

Grok 4.6 in Foundry represents a significant value-tier option for agentic, long-horizon AI development. Its selectable reasoning effort and straightforward integration make it an efficient choice for advanced AI applications.
